title: Fractions: Halves, Thirds, Quarters and Fifths
seo_title: Grade 2 Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use and name fractions in familiar contexts including halves, quarters, thirds and fifths; recognise fractions in diagrammatic form; solve and explain solutions to practical problems that involve equal sharing leading to solutions that include unitary fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 2 maths worksheets: halves, thirds, quarters and fifths of shapes and collections. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The parts must be equal.
  • A half is 1 of 2 equal parts; a third is 1 of 3; a quarter is 1 of 4; a fifth is 1 of 5.
  • More parts means smaller parts: a fifth is smaller than a half.
  • A quarter of 12 is 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

Examples

Example

A third of 15

15 ÷ 3

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Unequal partsThe parts must be the same size.
Bigger number, bigger partA fifth is smaller than a third.
The wrong divisorA quarter: divide by 4.

items.q: Which shape is cut into halves?
items.e: Halves are 2 equal parts. That is D. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. B has 3 equal parts. C has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into quarters?
items.e: Quarters are 4 equal parts. That is B. A has 4 parts, but they are not equal. C has 3 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into thirds?
items.e: Thirds are 3 equal parts. That is A. B has 3 parts, but they are not equal. C has 4 equal parts. D has 2 parts that are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is not cut into equal parts?
items.e: Look for parts that are different sizes. That is C. A has 4 equal parts. B has 2 equal parts. D has 3 equal parts.

items.q: How many quarters make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into quarters has 4 equal parts. So 4 quarters make 1 whole: 44 = 1.

items.q: How many halves make 1 whole?

items.q: How many thirds make 1 whole?

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Which is bigger: 12 of a cake or 14 of a cake?
items.e: Cut a cake into 2 and the pieces are big. Cut it into 4 and the pieces are smaller. So 12 is bigger.

items.q: What do we call 1 of 4 equal parts?
items.e: 4 equal parts are quarters. One part is one quarter, written 14.

items.q: What do we call 1 of 8 equal parts?

items.q: How do we write one half?
items.e: One half is 1 part out of 2 equal parts. The 1 goes on top and the 2 goes underneath: 12.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Nomsa eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: There are 4 equal slices, so each slice is a quarter. Nomsa eats 1 slice: 14.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Busisiwe eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: 4 − 1 = 3 slices are left out of 4 equal slices. That is 34.

items.q: There are 30 children in a Grade 2 class. Half of them have school dinners. How many children have school dinners?
items.e: Share 30 into 2 equal groups: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 children. One group is 12.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Share 60 into 4 equal parts: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60. So a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30: 30 + 30 = 60.

items.q: Precious has 8 pencils. 34 of them are red. How many red pencils are there?
items.e: First find 14: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. You need 3 groups, not 1: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 pencils.

items.q: 4 friends share 16 sweets equally. Each friend gets 14 of the sweets. How many sweets does each friend get?
items.e: Share 16 into 4 equal groups: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 sweets. One group is 14.

items.q: Kagiso has a ribbon 20 cm long. He cuts it in half. How long is each piece?

items.q: A box has 12 eggs. 34 of the eggs are brown. How many eggs are brown?

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Lindiwe eats 13 of one cake. Nadia eats 14 of the other cake. Who eats more?
items.e: A cake cut into 3 has bigger pieces than a cake cut into 4. 13 is bigger than 14, so Lindiwe eats more.

items.q: Two sandwiches are the same size. Palesa eats 12 of one. Sibusiso eats 24 of the other. Who eats more?
items.e: 24 = 12. Sibusiso has more pieces, but they are smaller. They eat the same amount.

items.q: Kgomotso has 20 apples. She gives away 14 of them. How many apples does she give away?

items.q: Zinhle has 20 grapes. She eats 14 of them. How many grapes are left?

items.q: There are 10 children in the playground. Half of them are girls. How many are boys?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5, so 5 are girls. The other half are boys: 10 − 5 = 5 boys.

items.q: Half of Amahle’s beads are blue. She has 9 blue beads. How many beads does she have altogether?
items.e: 9 beads are one half. The whole is 2 halves: 9 + 9 = 18 beads. Check: half of 18 is 9.

items.q: Lerato has 9 stickers. She gives 13 of them to Lungile. How many stickers does Lungile get?
items.e: Share 9 into 3 equal groups: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 stickers. One group is 13.
